official_sources.name: Austrian Federal Government (Migration.gv.at)
official_sources.description: Official legal portal for Austrian Student Residence Permits (Aufenthaltsbewilligung Student), 20 hrs/week student employment permissions, and the 12-month post-study Rot-Weiß-Rot (Red-White-Red) Karte job-seeker visa.

official_sources.name: OeAD - Austrian Agency for International Mobility
official_sources.description: Official national guidance for visa entry, country-specific document legalization paths (Apostille vs Superlegalization), accredited student housing, and national scholarship portal (grants.at).

official_sources.name: German Federal Foreign Office (Auswärtiges Amt)
official_sources.description: Official federal portal for German national student visas (Visum zu Studienzwecken), blocked account (Sperrkonto) statutory minimums (€11,904/year), and health insurance compliance.

official_sources.name: DAAD - German Academic Exchange Service
official_sources.description: Comprehensive admission database for German universities, official credential recognition standards (Anabin), and language certificate requirements.

official_sources.name: Uni-assist e.V.
official_sources.description: Official pre-evaluation service used by over 180 German universities for international Bachelor degree equivalency checks, preliminary documentation (VPD), and German grade conversion.

accepted_methods.method: Personal Bank Account in Student's Name
accepted_methods.details: Checking or savings account in applicant's name with immediate access in Austria or international account (convertible to EUR) showing full 12-month funds. Must provide proof of legal origin of funds (parents' salary slips, tax returns, sale of assets, or savings record).
A notarized Austrian liability declaration signed by an Austrian resident sponsor or EU guarantor, covering all living and accommodation costs, verified by Austrian immigration authorities.

accepted_methods.method: Official Austrian or International Scholarship (e.g., OeAD, Ernst Mach Grant)
accepted_methods.details: Official scholarship award letter from an accredited foundation (OeAD, Erasmus Mundus, Austrian government) proving monthly living stipend.

visa_and_permit.application_location: Austrian Embassy/Consulate in home country (for visa-required nationals) or directly at the local Immigration Authority (Magistrat MA 35 in Vienna, Bezirkshauptmannschaft in other federal states) within visa-free 90 days for visa-exempt nationals.
visa_and_permit.application_fee: €160 total (€120 at application submission, €20 at grant of permit, €20 personalization fee).
visa_and_permit.processing_time: Normally 60 to 90 days from complete document submission.

work_rights.working_hours: Up to 20 hours per week during ongoing semesters (unrestricted during semester holidays).
work_rights.post_study_visa: Rot-Weiß-Rot Karte (Red-White-Red Card) for Graduates: 12-month job seeker residence permit granted immediately upon Master graduation with no labor market test (Ersatzkraftverfahren) required once an adequate skilled job offer with minimum statutory gross salary is secured.

health_insurance.coverage: Comprehensive universal health coverage across all Austrian public doctors, clinics, and university hospitals.
health_insurance.visa_entry_requirement: For entering Austria to pick up your residence permit, an incoming travel health insurance covering at least €30,000 (e.g., Mawista, Care Concept, or Allianz) is required until ÖGK registration is activated.

financial_proof.title: German Blocked Account (Sperrkonto)
accepted_alternatives: Formal Obligation (Verpflichtungserklärung pursuant to §§ 66-68 AufenthG) issued by an alien authority in Germany.
Recognized scholarship from public funds (e.g. DAAD, Alexander von Humboldt, Erasmus+).

visa_and_permit.permit_name: National Visa for Study Purposes (Visum zu Studienzwecken, Category D)
visa_and_permit.application_location: German Embassy or Visa Application Center (VFS Global / TLScontact) in student's country of residence.
visa_and_permit.processing_time: Normally 4 to 12 weeks depending on embassy appointment backlogs.

work_rights.working_hours: 140 full days or 280 half days per calendar year (approximately 20 hours per week during term time).
work_rights.post_study_visa: 18-month Job Seeker Residence Permit (Aufenthaltserlaubnis zur Arbeitsplatzsuche nach § 20 Abs. 3 Nr. 1 AufenthG) upon graduating with a German Master's degree, leading directly to the EU Blue Card (Blaue Karte EU).

health_insurance.provider: Statutory Public Health Insurance (Gesetzliche Krankenversicherung - GKV)
health_insurance.monthly_cost: Approx. €125 - €130 / month (discounted student tariff up to age 30).
health_insurance.coverage: Full medical, dental, hospitalization, and prescription coverage without deductible.

checklist_items.title: Valid Biometric Passport
checklist_items.description: Must be valid for at least 6 months beyond intended stay in Europe, contain at least 2 consecutive blank pages, and have been issued within the last 10 years.

checklist_items.title: Biometric Passport Photographs (35x45mm)
checklist_items.description: Recent (taken within the last 6 months), front-facing, neutral facial expression, plain light grey/white background, compliant with international ICAO biometric standards.

checklist_items.title: Official Birth Certificate with Legalization & Translation
checklist_items.description: Full birth certificate stating parents' names. Must carry Hague Apostille OR Diplomatic Superlegalization by the Austrian/German embassy in country of issuance, accompanied by certified translation into German or English by a court-sworn translator.

checklist_items.title: Bachelor Degree Certificate (Diploma)
checklist_items.description: Original degree parchment or provisional degree certificate indicating completion of a recognized Bachelor program (minimum 180 ECTS or 3-4 years). Must be properly legalized according to bilateral agreements.

checklist_items.title: Official Academic Transcripts of Records
checklist_items.description: Complete semester-by-semester breakdown of all completed courses, examination grades, credit hours, and GPA, bearing university seal and registrar signature.

checklist_items.title: Course Descriptions / Curriculum Module Catalog (Modulhandbuch)
checklist_items.description: Official university syllabus detailing learning objectives, lecture/lab hours, and weekly topics covered in your Bachelor's degree. Essential for Austrian (UG 2002 § 64) and German equivalence checks in mathematics, algorithms, and theoretical computer science.

checklist_items.title: APS Certificate (Akademische Prüfstelle)
checklist_items.description: Mandatory authenticity certificate issued by the German Embassy APS bureau. Required for all applicants with Bachelor degrees from India, China, or Vietnam before applying to German universities or student visas.
checklist_items.authority: APS India / APS China / APS Vietnam

checklist_items.title: Certified English Language Test (IELTS / TOEFL / Cambridge)
checklist_items.description: Official score report: IELTS Academic (overall 6.5–7.0, sub-bands 6.0+) or TOEFL iBT (88–100 points, minimum 20 per section). Medium of Instruction (MOI) certificates are accepted only for graduates of English-speaking native countries (UK, USA, CA, AU, NZ) or specific exempt universities.

checklist_items.title: Proof of Sufficient Funds (Sperrkonto / Bank Balance Proof)
checklist_items.description: For Germany: Confirmed Blocked Account (Sperrkonto) with €11,904. For Austria: Bank statement showing full 12 months (€14,615 if 24+) in student's name with source of funds documentation, or notarized Austrian liability declaration (Haftungserklärung).

checklist_items.title: Police Clearance Certificate (PCC / Strafregisterbescheinigung)
checklist_items.description: Criminal record certificate issued by national police or Ministry of Interior of your country of citizenship and recent country of residence. Must be issued within the last 3 months, legalized with Apostille/Superlegalization, and sworn translated.

checklist_items.title: Comprehensive Health Insurance Coverage
checklist_items.description: Proof of statutory or approved comprehensive health insurance coverage without exclusions. Austria: ÖGK student insurance (€69.13/mo) + travel incoming policy for visa entry. Germany: TK / AOK public health insurance (€125/mo).

checklist_items.title: Proof of Accommodation (Rental Contract / OeAD Housing)
checklist_items.description: Formal tenancy agreement (Mietvertrag), student dormitory contract (OeAD-WohnraumverwaltungsGmbH in Austria, Studentenwerk in Germany), or landlord confirmation for at least the initial 3 to 6 months.

ielts.name: IELTS Academic
ielts.top_tier_requirement: Overall 7.0 (Writing/Speaking min 6.5) for TUM, TU Wien, Uni Vienna
ielts.acceptance: Universally accepted at 100% of Austrian and German universities

toefl.name: TOEFL iBT
toefl.acceptance: Universally accepted. Note: 'Home Edition' is rejected by certain technical faculties.

cambridge.name: Cambridge C1 Advanced (CAE) & C2 Proficiency (CPE)
cambridge.validity: Accepted indefinitely or within 2-3 years depending on university regulation

pte.name: PTE Academic (Pearson Test of English)
pte.acceptance: Widely accepted at TU Graz, JKU Linz, and leading German universities

moi_rules.title: Medium of Instruction (MOI) Exemption Policy
moi_rules.rule_summary: Most premier universities (TUM, TU Wien, Uni Vienna, RWTH Aachen) do NOT accept a simple MOI letter from non-native English-speaking countries. An MOI waiver is only granted if you completed your entire Bachelor's in a recognized native English-speaking country (Australia, Canada, Ireland, New Zealand, UK, USA).

austrian_scale.label: Sehr gut
austrian_scale.description: Outstanding performance with no major flaws.

austrian_scale.label: Gut
austrian_scale.description: Generally sound performance with minor flaws.

german_scale.label: Sehr gut
german_scale.admission_competitiveness: Extremely High (TUM, TU Wien priority shortlist)

german_scale.label: Befriedigend
german_scale.admission_competitiveness: May require additional aptitude interview or test

german_scale.label: Ausreichend
german_scale.admission_competitiveness: Borderline / Minimum threshold for university matriculation

bavarian_formula.name: Modified Bavarian Formula (Modifizierte bayerische Formel)
bavarian_formula.legal_basis: Resolution of the Standing Conference of the Ministers of Education and Cultural Affairs of the Länder (KMK) / Bavarian Higher Education Act

variables.N: Calculated German/Austrian equivalent grade (1.0 = best, 4.0 = passing threshold)
variables.N_max: Maximum possible score/grade in your country's grading system
variables.N_min: Minimum passing score/grade required to graduate in your system
variables.N_d: Applicant's actual Bachelor degree score or GPA

course_descriptions_guide.title: How to Prepare Your Course Descriptions / Module Catalog (Modulhandbuch)
course_descriptions_guide.importance: European university admissions boards (Austrian UG 2002 § 64 and German KMK guidelines) do NOT admit based on degree title alone. They perform a credit-by-credit equivalence audit against their specific Bachelor's curriculum.

core_subject_clusters.subject: Higher Mathematics & Statistics
core_subject_clusters.topics: Calculus, Linear Algebra, Multivariable Calculus, Discrete Mathematics, Probability & Statistics

core_subject_clusters.subject: Theoretical Computer Science & Algorithms
core_subject_clusters.topics: Data Structures, Algorithm Analysis, Automata Theory, Formal Languages, Complexity (P vs NP)

core_subject_clusters.subject: Practical Computer Science & Systems
core_subject_clusters.topics: Object-Oriented Programming, Operating Systems, Computer Architecture, Computer Networks, Database Systems

core_subject_clusters.subject: Software Engineering & Project Work
core_subject_clusters.topics: Software Architecture, Agile Methods, Git, Testing & Quality Assurance, Team Capstone Project

preparation_checklist: Obtain the official university-published Module Handbook or Course Catalog.
Ensure each course description specifies: course title, course code, weekly hours (lecture vs lab), total credit hours or ECTS equivalent.
List the syllabus breakdown: detailed weekly lecture topics, algorithmic methods taught, and mathematical proofs covered.
Include prescribed literature and textbooks (author, title, publisher).
Have the document officially certified: university stamp, seal, and signature of the Dean/Registrar, or provide an active official university URL pointing to the archived public curriculum.
